subject: Private VPC deployment - networking questions & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc:  
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment - networking questions & next steps

Alex, thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Recap:
- You confirmed FinLytics wants a private deployment (Private VPC) for production data, driven by compliance and internal network controls.
- Preferred cloud: AWS (us-east-1) with a requirement that Redwood endpoints not be publicly routable from the internet.
- Primary concerns: restricted egress, IP allowlists, and avoiding cross-account exposure.

To move to a technical design, we need a few network details from your team so our solutions engineers can prepare a PrivateLink design:
- Do you prefer AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint) or VPC Peering? (You mentioned PrivateLink as a possibility on the call.)
- AWS Account ID(s) we should provision endpoints into (one per environment: prod/staging).
- VPC CIDR(s) + preferred subnets for endpoints (public/private).
- Route table and security group constraints (any restrictive NACLs or outbound proxy requirements).
- Any IP allowlist or static egress IP requirements on your side.
- Expected peak RPS and average connection duration (helps size endpoints).
- TLS termination preference (Redwood manages certs or you provide).
- Any corporate firewall or vendor onboarding docs we should follow.

Attachments: I've attached our Private VPC networking checklist and a short FAQ that explains differences between PrivateLink and peering. I've also included a draft SOW for the environment work if you want an early look.

Next steps:
1) If you can share the AWS account IDs, CIDRs, and your netops contact, we'll schedule a tech call with our Solutions Engineer (Rishi) and Network lead (Vivek).
2) Proposed times: Fri 07/31 10:00-11:00 ET or Mon 08/03 14:00-15:00 ET, which works best?

Thanks; happy to coordinate on calendar.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-faq.pdf, networking-checklist.xlsx, sow-draft.docx

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics Network Team <netops@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - networking questions & next steps

Marissa, thanks for the recap and the materials. Confirming a few items from our side:

- We are leaning toward AWS PrivateLink rather than peering because it aligns better with our security posture and avoids cross-account route table changes.
- Primary AWS region: us-east-1. We will provide account IDs for prod and staging by EOD tomorrow.
- Regarding IP allowlists: our security team prefers not to rely on public IPs. We need to understand whether Redwood will require any inbound public IPs or whether PrivateLink covers all traffic (app -> Redwood).
- Throughput: peak ~120 req/s, average ~35 req/s, typical request duration 300-600ms.
- Procurement timeline: vendor review and legal sign-off expected by mid-August.

I've copied our netops alias for the technical call (netops@finlytics.com). Can Rishi and Vivek confirm whether PrivateLink will remove the need to maintain allowlists of Redwood public egress IPs? Also, do you support static IPs for egress if we were to use a different deployment mode later?

Good to see the SOW; we'll review. For meeting time, Fri 07/31 10:00 ET works for our team.

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Product Manager, FinLytics
alex.chen@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, FinLytics Network Team <netops@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - networking questions & next steps

Alex, great, thanks. Quick answers before the tech call:

- PrivateLink summary: yes, with AWS PrivateLink, traffic from your VPC goes to a VPC endpoint; there is no public IP surface for inbound requests to Redwood. That typically eliminates the need to maintain a public allowlist for our endpoints. We'll confirm specifics in the tech call.
- Static egress IPs: PrivateLink customers do not need to rely on Redwood public egress IPs for inbound traffic. If you later choose a Dedicated deployment with outbound egress through your VPC, we can provide guidance on static egress options (NAT/Gateway + egress IP planning) but it's a different architecture.

Checklist (what we'll ask netops to provide ahead of the call):
- AWS Account ID(s) for prod + staging
- VPC CIDR(s) and preferred subnets for endpoint ENIs
- Route table IDs where endpoints can be associated
- Any proxy or egress NAT requirement (corporate HTTP proxy)
- Whether your firewall inspects TLS (SNI) or expects SSL passthrough
- Point-of-contact for cert/key exchange or ARN if you'll manage certs

I'll let Rishi and Vivek take the rest on the tech call. Meeting confirmed for Fri 07/31 10:00 ET. I'll send a calendar invite with the agenda and a short pre-read.


Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, FinLytics Network Team <netops@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private VPC deployment - networking questions & next steps

Alex / Netops: quick technical notes ahead of Friday's call so we can make it actionable:

1) PrivateLink behavior: inbound requests to Redwood over PrivateLink stay inside AWS backbone between your VPC endpoint and our VPC endpoint service. You should not need to add any public IP allowlist for inbound traffic.

2) Ports & protocols: we use TLS over TCP 443 for all traffic. If your firewall blocks SNI, please let us know; we can support alternate routing but that's uncommon.

3) DNS: for PrivateLink we'll provide a service DNS name (vpc.<env>.svc.redwood-inference.internal) and instructions to create an endpoint DNS override if needed.

4) Certificates: Redwood can manage TLS certificates for the endpoint service; if you must provide certs, send the ACM ARN or cert bundle and we'll update the design.

5) Monitoring & throughput: based on the numbers Alex provided (peak ~120 rps), PrivateLink endpoints in us-east-1 with our default configuration should be sufficient. If you expect large attachment uploads, tell us estimated payload sizes.

6) SOW & timeline: attached a short draft SOW with network tasks and an estimated two-week provisioning window after account details are finalized.

Looking forward to Friday - please attach the AWS account IDs and any sample route table/security group rules so we can sketch the exact steps.


Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: sow-draft.docx
